message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means the holiday falls on a weekday and the adjacent weekend days create a 3‑day break.)

| Holiday | Observed Date (2023) | Long‑Weekend Span (Saturday – Monday) | Notes |
|---------|---------------------|---------------------------------------|-------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 2 (observed; Jan 1 was Sunday) | Jan 1 – 3 | 3‑day break (Sunday–Tuesday) |
| Family Day (Ontario, BC, AB, SK, NB, PE) | Feb 20 (Monday) | Feb 18 – 20 | 3‑day break (Saturday–Monday) |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Friday) | Apr 7 – 9 | 3‑day break (Friday–Sunday) |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | May 20 – 22 | 3‑day break (Saturday–Monday) |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Saturday) | Jul 1 – 3 | 3‑day break (Saturday–Sunday) |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Monday) | Sep 2 – 4 | 3‑day break (Saturday–Monday) |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 (Monday) | Oct 7 – 9 | 3‑day break (Saturday–Monday) |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 (Monday) | Nov 9 – 11 | 3‑day break (Saturday–Monday) |
| Christmas & Boxing Day | Dec 25 (Monday) & Dec 26 (Tuesday) | Dec 24 – 26 | 3‑day break (Saturday–Monday) |

**Key points**

- **New Year’s Day** falls on a Sunday in 2023, so the holiday is observed on Monday, giving a 3‑day break from Sunday to Tuesday.
- **Canada Day** falls on a Saturday, so the holiday itself is on Saturday, creating a 3‑day break from Saturday to Sunday.
- **Christmas & Boxing Day** together form a long weekend from Saturday, Dec 24, through Monday, Dec 26.
- Some provinces have additional holidays (e.g., Family Day in Alberta, Saskatchewan, etc.), but the above list covers the federal holidays that create long weekends across Canada.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app!
